title: Tamil Nadu Politics – Evening Brief – 26 November 2026
headline: DMK Moves Madras High Court Demanding CBI Probe Into Kallakurichi Collector Harassment Scandal Involving TVK MLA

sections.big_picture:
Tamil Nadu's political landscape is currently dominated by intense fallout surrounding the alleged sexual harassment of a senior woman district official by Kallakurichi TVK MLA Arul Vignesh. The scandal has triggered a fierce multi-party confrontation, with the principal opposition DMK moving the Madras High Court to demand a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe, alleging institutional cover-ups by the Chief Minister's Office and the Chief Secretary's department. Meanwhile, the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) administration under Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay faces mounting pressure from both the AIADMK—which has announced state-wide protests for December 2—and internal coalition fissures, even as the government rolls out progressive welfare measures such as mandatory paternity leave and rehabilitation housing.

Simultaneously, anti-corruption crackdowns have intensified with the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption arresting key political aides in multi-crore tender malpractices, while opposition leaders question the integrity of ongoing state-led investigations. As political realignments take shape and regional parties clash over judicial oversight versus state investigative competence, the governance framework in Tamil Nadu remains deeply polarized. These compounding controversies underscore a volatile legislative and administrative climate across the state, setting the stage for aggressive public agitations and intense legal battles in the upcoming weeks.

top_developments.headline: DMK Files Writ Petition in Madras High Court Demanding CBI Investigation Against TVK MLA Over Collector Harassment
top_developments.summary: Former DMK MP Dr. Kanimozhi NVN Somu has formally filed a writ petition in the Madras High Court demanding a comprehensive Central Bureau of Investigation probe into the alleged sexual harassment of the Kallakurichi District Collector by TVK legislator C. Arul Vignesh. The petition contends that state authorities, including the Chief Minister and the Chief Secretary, deliberately delayed initiating criminal proceedings under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, despite possessing actionable intelligence for nearly four months. sections.government_and_administration: - **Tamil Nadu Government Introduces 15 Days of Paternity Leave for Married Male Employees and Inaugurates Welfare Housing:** In a progressive administrative policy shift, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay announced the immediate implementation of 15 days of paid paternity leave for married male employees across all state government departments. According to the official government order released on November 26, 2026, eligible employees can utilize this leave entitlement either 15 days prior to the expected date of childbirth or within a six-month window following delivery. Simultaneously, the Chief Minister inaugurated 148 newly constructed residential units for Sri Lankan Tamils at the Pambar Dam rehabilitation camp in Krishnagiri district via video conferencing from the Secretariat. Funded at a total project cost of ₹8.52 crore, with an additional ₹1.37 crore allocated for foundational civic infrastructure, these housing units aim to uplift displaced families. Furthermore, the administration initiated the direct disbursal of enhanced monthly financial assistance supporting 56,638 individuals across 19,710 families residing in rehabilitation camps statewide, reinforcing the ruling TVK's welfare agenda amidst mounting political friction. ([The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/tamil-nadu-introduced-15-days-of-paternity-leave-for-married-government-employees/article71745892.ece))
sections.political_parties_and_opposition: - **AIADMK Announces Statewide Protests Over Law and Order Failures While Opposition Slams TVK Administration:** Escalating its direct confrontation with the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam government, the AIADMK has officially announced a massive statewide protest demonstration scheduled for December 2, 2026. Party General Secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami stated that the demonstrations will condemn the government's severe lapses in maintaining law and order, rising administrative corruption, and mishandling of high-profile bureaucratic misconduct cases. The announcement follows intense verbal sparring across political platforms, where opposition leaders like DMK youth wing leader Udhayanidhi Stalin accused Chief Minister Vijay of directly shielding Kallakurichi MLA Arul Vignesh from criminal prosecution after he allegedly sent inappropriate text messages to a female District Collector. Simultaneously, Congress State President Manickam Tagore publicly questioned the DMK's shifting stance, asking whether the party had surrendered to the Governor after previously criticizing him as a mere postman, following Udhayanidhi Stalin's formal submission of a petition to Governor R.N. Arlekar. Meanwhile, the VCK, led by Thol. Thirumavalavan, publicly distanced itself from the demand for a central agency probe, asserting that the state police apparatus is entirely capable of delivering a transparent and lawful investigation. ([The Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/chennai/aiadmk-to-hold-state-wide-protest-in-tamil-nadu-on-dec-2-to-highlight-failures-of-tvk-govt/articleshow/136196105.cms))
sections.assembly_courts_and_policy: - **DVAC Arrests Senior DMK Leader K.N. Nehru's Aide in Multi-Crore Municipal Tender Scam:** The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) has executed a high-profile arrest, taking Kavi Prasad—a close associate of former Minister and senior DMK leader K.N. Nehru—into custody in connection with an ongoing multi-crore tender scam. The Special Investigation Cell of the DVAC acted weeks after formally registering an FIR on September 4, 2026, targeting widespread financial irregularities and cartelization in the award of Municipal Administration and Water Supply (MAWS) Department contracts between 2021 and 2025. Investigators allege that the syndicate manipulated procurement processes, subverted statutory bidding guidelines, and funneled public funds through shell entities linked to key political operatives. The arrest has sent shockwaves through opposition DMK ranks, who have condemned the action as politically motivated state-sponsored victimization designed to deflect public attention from the ruling TVK government's administrative failures. Legal experts anticipate that the Special Investigation Cell will seek extended judicial custody for the accused as financial auditors pore through seized digital evidence and departmental files spanning multiple municipal corporations across Tamil Nadu. ([The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/dvac-arrests-kn-nehrus-close-aide-kavi-prasad-in-multi-crore-tender-scam/article71747806.ece))
sections.district_developments: - **Kallakurichi District Administration Faces Dual Political Storm Following Harassment FIRs Against Legislators:** The administrative machinery in Kallakurichi district has been thrown into acute turmoil following consecutive criminal cases registered against prominent local legislators within a single week. Following the filing of charges against TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh under five stringent sections—including harassment of women—for allegedly transmitting inappropriate electronic communications to the District Collector, local law enforcement booked Rishivandiyam DMK MLA Vasantham Karthikeyan under three similar legal sections based on a separate harassment complaint lodged by a female government officer. The Madras High Court has mandated strict judicial oversight, appointing Inspector General of Police I.G. Kamini and investigating officer Shrishti Singh to spearhead an impartial inquiry into the allegations surrounding the district administration. The unprecedented convergence of corruption and harassment allegations against lawmakers from both ruling and opposition parties has paralyzed routine administrative functions in Kallakurichi, prompting civil service associations to demand enhanced legal protections and secure working environments for executive officers operating at the grassroots level. ([The Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/chennai/rishivandiyam-dmk-mla-booked-for-harassing-woman-officer-in-kallakurichi/articleshow/136200220.cms))
sections.what_to_watch_next: Over the next 24 to 48 hours, political observers will closely monitor the Madras High Court's proceedings regarding the DMK's writ petition seeking a CBI inquiry into the Kallakurichi collector harassment case. Key developments will also center around preparations for the AIADMK's statewide protests scheduled for December 2, alongside anticipated counter-statements from the ruling TVK leadership. Additionally, legal arguments in the DVAC corruption case involving the arrest of K.N. Nehru's aide are expected to unfold in subordinate courts, setting a contentious tone for upcoming legislative sessions.
